why_scored: OpenCode's own voice is a GPT-Live call that needs a paid OpenAI API key or a paid OpenCode Console account, and it only steers OpenCode sessions, so it cannot run free or type into another app. Hex (anomalyco/hex) is the OpenCode team's local dictation app; it runs free and headless on Linux, so it is scored in its place, with its default English model.

engines.silas: Silas, Parakeet v3 (int8 ONNX), through the dictation path (silas-bench run)
engines.rival: Hex 3.4.0 release binary, Parakeet Unified English 0.6B Q8_0 GGUF on transcribe.cpp, CPU (bench/engines/hex_engine.py)
engines.opencode_voice: OpenCode Desktop voice call: gpt-live-1 over WebRTC, delegating to gpt-6.1-sol (not run: paid key)

machine.name: chapel1
machine.gpu: none used (Hex fell back to its CPU engine; Silas runs on CPU)

silas_real_time.how: silas-bench run, paced in real time (times)

rival_service.how: bench/engines/hex_engine.py: a warm `hex service`, one `hex transcribe` per clip (times and accuracy)

rival_one_shot.how: bench/engines/hex_engine.py --one-shot: no service (accuracy only; Hex keeps its better run per metric)

time_to_first_word_ms.what: median, key down to the first text available. Silas: its first piece or its final text. Hex's file path is batch: clip length plus its wait.
time_to_first_word_ms.opencode_voice_note: not measured: needs a paid key. A GPT-Live call streams, but its words go to a voice agent, not to a text field.

wait_after_key_up_ms.what: median, key up to the final text: the wait users feel
wait_after_key_up_ms.opencode_voice_note: not measured: needs a paid key

wait_after_key_up_p95_ms.what: 95th percentile of the same wait; the long clips
wait_after_key_up_p95_ms.opencode_voice_note: not measured: needs a paid key

wer.what: word error rate on ref_verbatim, pooled over the subset's speech clips (score.py's default normalization)
wer.opencode_voice_note: not measured: gpt-live-1 is a paid cloud model with no free tier in the source

punctuation_f1.what: F1 of sentence marks (comma, stop, question) on ref_formatted, words aligned (rivals.py)
punctuation_f1.opencode_voice_note: not measured: its text is rewritten by an agent before a session sees it

formatted_error.what: token error rate on ref_formatted, case and punctuation counted (score.py)

typing_ms.what: median time to put each clip's final text into the focused app on X11 (Xvfb). Silas: measured, its typer at the default "fast" pace. Hex: modeled from its source, one Ctrl+V after a clipboard write, timed as one key event by the same typer.
typing_ms.opencode_voice_note: none: a call never puts text in another app; its delegate sends messages to OpenCode sessions only

setup_steps.what: user actions on Linux from nothing to the first dictation (setup.steps lists each, with its source)
setup_steps.opencode_voice_note: plus a paid OpenAI or OpenCode Console account

peak_rss_mb.what: peak resident memory of the process holding the model
peak_rss_mb.opencode_voice_note: the model runs on OpenAI's servers

cpu_s_per_audio_min.what: CPU seconds per minute of audio, all threads: the battery proxy
cpu_s_per_audio_min.opencode_voice_note: the model runs on OpenAI's servers

silas_steps.step: paste the one-line installer into a terminal; it installs Silas and opens it
silas_steps.quote: Paste one line into a terminal. It downloads Silas, installs it and opens it.

silas_no_step.what: the speech model downloads by itself
silas_no_step.quote: The speech model (478 MB) starts downloading right away.
Windows asks for nothing. On Linux the installer

rival_steps.step: open Hex from the launcher (the script does not open it); the first run downloads the model

setup.rival_steps_note: On a Wayland desktop without the GlobalShortcuts portal, binding the shortcut in the desktop's own keybindings is one more step (docs/linux.md:530-536).

opencode_voice_steps.step: install an OpenCode Desktop build that is not the prod channel
turn on the Voice calls experiment in the developer Knobs panel (off by default)
give the server an OpenAI API key or an OpenCode Console sign-in (both paid; a ChatGPT sign-in is refused)
